    input rst,
    input [4:0] in,
    output reg [4:0] out
);

    // First stage: doubling the input
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            stage1 <= 5'b0;
        end else begin
            stage1 <= in << 1; // Double the input
        end

    end
endmodule

description: Create a Carry-Skip Adder (CSA) in Verilog. The CSA should take two n-bit binary numbers as inputs and produce their sum along with a carry output. Implement functionality such that it can handle carry skip operations efficiently.
code:
module carry_skip_adder #(parameter N = 8) (
    input [N-1:0] A,
    input [N-1:0] B,
    input Cin,
    output [N-1:0] Sum,
    output Cout
);
    wire [N:0] C; // Carry signals
    wire [N-1:0] P; // Propagate signals
    wire [N-1:0] G; // Generate signals

    assign P = A ^ B; // Propagate
    assign G = A & B; // Generate

    assign C[0] = Cin; // Initial carry input
    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin : carry_logic
            assign C[i+1] = G[i] | (P[i] & C[i]); // Carry generation
        end
    endgenerate

    assign Sum = P ^ C[N-1:0]; // Sum output
    assign Cout = C[N]; // Final carry out

endmodule

description: Design a 8x Phase Locked Loop (PLL) circuit in Verilog that takes a clock input and generates an output clock that is 8 times the frequency of the input clock. The PLL should also have a reset functionality that resets the generated clock signal to a known state.
code:
module pll_8x (
    input wire clk_in,       // Input clock
    input wire reset,        // Reset signal
    output reg clk_out       // Output clock (8x)
);

reg [2:0] counter;           // 3-bit counter for 8x frequency
parameter DIVISOR = 8;       // Divisor to achieve 8x frequency

always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        counter <= 3'b0;
        clk_out <= 1'b0;     // Reset output clock
    end else begin
        counter <= counter + 1;
        if (counter == DIVISOR - 1) begin
            clk_out <= ~clk_out; // Toggle output clock
            counter <= 3'b0; // Reset counter
        end
    end
end

endmodule

);

description:
Create an SPI master controller that sends a byte of data to a SPI slave. The controller should have the following inputs and outputs:
- Input: clk (clock), rst (reset), start (signal to start transmission), mosi (data to be sent), 
- Output: miso (data received from the slave), sclk (serial clock), cs (chip select).
The controller should send a byte of data over MOSI, generate a clock signal on SCLK, and receive data on MISO when the transmission is complete.
code:
module spi_master (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input [7:0] mosi,
    output reg miso,
    output reg sclk,
    output reg cs
);
    reg [2:0] state;
    reg [2:0] bit_cnt;
    reg [7:0] data_reg;

    localparam IDLE = 3'b000, 
               SEND = 3'b001, 
               SCLK_HIGH = 3'b010, 
               SCLK_LOW = 3'b011, 
               RECEIVE = 3'b100, 
               DONE = 3'b101;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            sclk <= 0;
            cs <= 1;
            bit_cnt <= 0;
            data_reg <= 0;
            miso <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    cs <= 1; // Chip select inactive
                    if (start) begin
                        data_reg <= mosi; // Load data to send
                        cs <= 0; // Chip select active
                        state <= SEND;
                    end
                end
                SEND: begin
                    if (bit_cnt < 8) begin
                        miso <= data_reg[7 - bit_cnt]; // Send MSB first
                        state <= SCLK_LOW; // Move to clock generation
                    end else begin
                        state <= DONE; // Finished sending
                    end
                end
                SCLK_LOW: begin
                    sclk <= 0; // SCLK low
                    state <= SCLK_HIGH; // Move to SCLK high
                end
                SCLK_HIGH: begin
                    sclk <= 1; // SCLK high
                    bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1; // Increment bit counter
                    state <= SEND; // Go back to sending
                end
                DONE: begin
                    cs <= 1; // Chip select inactive
                    bit_cnt <= 0; // Reset bit counter
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design an 8-bit ALU that can perform the following operations based on a 3-bit control signal: 
000 - Addition,
001 - Subtraction,
010 - AND,
011 - OR,
100 - XOR,
101 - NOT (Unary operation where A is treated as A and all bits are inverted),
110 - Increment,
111 - Decrement. 
The ALU should take two 8-bit inputs A and B, and produce an 8-bit output Y.
code:
module ALU (
    input [7:0] A,
    input [7:0] B,
    input [2:0] ctrl,
    output reg [7:0] Y
);
    always @(*) begin
        case (ctrl)
            3'b000: Y = A + B;              // Addition
            3'b001: Y = A - B;              // Subtraction
            3'b010: Y = A & B;              // AND
            3'b011: Y = A | B;              // OR
            3'b100: Y = A ^ B;              // XOR
            3'b101: Y = ~A;                 // NOT
            3'b110: Y = A + 1;              // Increment
            3'b111: Y = A - 1;              // Decrement
            default: Y = 8'b00000000;       // Default case
        endcase
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 16-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) with a polynomial feedback configuration. The LFSR should take a clock input and reset input.     input [7:0] dividend,
    input [3:0] divisor,

    output reg [3:0] remainder,
    output reg done
);

    reg [3:0] Q; // Quotient
    reg [3:0] M; // Divisor
    reg [3:0] count;
    reg state; // 0 for idle, 1 for dividing

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (start) begin
            A <= dividend; // Load dividend
            M <= divisor;  // Load divisor
            Q <= 0;        // Clear quotient
            count <= 8;    // Set count to width of dividend
            state <= 1;    // Start dividing
            done <= 0;     // Reset done signal
        end else if (state) begin
            if (count > 0) begin
                {A, Q} <= {A[7:0], Q[3:0]} - {4'b0, M}; // Subtract M
                if (A[7]) begin
                    A <= {A[7:0], Q[3:0]} + {4'b0, M}; // Restore A
                    Q <= {Q[3:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left and append 0
                end else begin
                    Q <= {Q[3:0], 1'b1}; // Shift left and append 1
                end
                count <= count - 1; // Decrement count
            end else begin
                quotient <= Q; // Output quotient
                remainder <= A[3:0]; // Output remainder
                done <= 1; // Indicate operation done
                state <= 0; // Go to idle
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    output reg [NUM_BLOCKS-1:0] status // Status of each block (1: allocated, 0: free)  
);

- Output '00' for a current level of 0 to 2.  
- Output '01' for a current level of 3 to 5.  
- Output '10' for a current level of 6 to 7.  
- Output '11' for a current level of 8 to 10.  
If the input exceeds this range, the output should be '11' (indicating an overflow condition).
code:
module current_sensor(  
    input [2:0] current_in,  
    output reg [1:0] current_out  
);  
    always @(*) begin  
        case (current_in)  
            3'b000, 3'b001, 3'b010: current_out = 2'b00; // 0 to 2  
            3'b011, 3'b100, 3'b101: current_out = 2'b01; // 3 to 5  
            3'b110, 3'b111: current_out = 2'b10; // 6 to 7  
            default: current_out = 2'b11; // 8 to 10 and overflow  
        endcase  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a 24-bit DAC (Digital-to-Analog Converter) that takes a 24-bit binary input and outputs a corresponding analog voltage level. The output voltage should be a scaled version of the input, with a range of 0V to Vref (where Vref is an external reference voltage provided as a parameter). The conversion should be done using a simple binary-weighted method.
code:
module DAC_24bit (

    input [11:0] Vref,           // 12-bit reference voltage (0 to 4095)
    output reg [11:0] analog_output // 12-bit analog output voltage level (0 to 4095)
);

    always @(*) begin
        analog_output = (digital_input * Vref) >> 12; // Scale the digital input with the reference voltage
    end
endmodule

description: Design an Automatic Repeat reQuest (ARQ) error correction system using a simple stop-and-wait protocol. The system should include a sender and a receiver. The sender sends a 5-bit data packet and waits for an acknowledgment (ACK) from the receiver. If the receiver detects an error in the received packet (using a parity bit), it sends a negative acknowledgment (NACK) back to the sender, which resends the packet. The receiver will be able to detect errors based on a parity bit check. The design should include state machines for the sender and the receiver.
code:
module arq_system (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [4:0] data_in,
    input error,
    output reg [4:0] data_out,
    output reg ack
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 0: idle, 1: send, 2: wait, 3: ack

    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, SEND = 2'b01, WAIT = 2'b10, ACK = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            data_out <= 5'b0;
            ack <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    state <= SEND;
                end
                SEND: begin
                    data_out <= data_in; // Send data
                    state <= WAIT;
                end
                WAIT: begin
                    if (error) begin
                        ack <= 0; // NACK
                        state <= SEND; // Resend data
                    end else begin
                        ack <= 1; // ACK
                        state <= ACK;
                    end
                end
                ACK: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple AES encryption circuit that takes a 128-bit plaintext input and a 128-bit key input to produce a 128-bit ciphertext output. The AES circuit should implement the first round of AES encryption, which consists of SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, and AddRoundKey operations.

Create a frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by a factor of 4. The output should toggle every 4 clock cycles. The circuit should also have an asynchronous reset that resets the output to 0.

Design a hazard detection and resolution circuit for a simple 2-input multiplexer. The multiplexer selects one of two inputs based on a select signal. However, if there are changes in the input signals while the select signal is stable, a hazard may occur. Your task is to implement a hazard-free multiplexer using a combination of gates to ensure stable output.

Design a 32-bit serializer that takes a 32-bit parallel input and serializes it into a single output bit stream. The design should have a clock input to manage the serialization process. The output should shift out one bit on each clock cycle.
code:
module serializer_32bit(  
    input wire clk,  
    input wire [31:0] parallel_in,  
    output reg serial_out  
);  
    reg [4:0] count; // 5 bits to count from 0 to 31  
     
    always @(posedge clk) begin  
        if (count < 32) begin  
            serial_out <= parallel_in[count];  
            count <= count + 1;  
        end else begin  
            count <= 0; // Reset count after all bits are serialized  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description:
Design a simple I2C controller with the following specifications:
- The controller has an input to receive a 7-bit I2C address and a 3-bit command (read, write, or stop).
- The controller should generate an acknowledgment (ACK) signal after sending the address.
- The output should indicate the current state of the controller (IDLE, ADDRESS_SENT, DATA_TRANSFER, ACK_RECEIVED).
- The controller should transition states based on the commands received.

Design a temperature sensor circuit that takes a 5-bit binary input representing a temperature value and outputs a signal indicating whether the temperature exceeds a predefined threshold. The threshold will be set to 25 (in decimal). The output signal should be 1 if the temperature is above the threshold and 0 otherwise. The circuit should also have a reset functionality to reset the output signal.
code:
module temperature_sensor (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [4:0] temperature,
    output reg over_threshold
);
    parameter THRESHOLD = 5'b11001; // 25 in binary

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            over_threshold <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (temperature > THRESHOLD) begin
                over_threshold <= 1;
            end else begin
                over_threshold <= 0;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a 4-bit DRAM cell that allows writing and reading of data. The DRAM cell should have a write enable signal (WE), a clock signal (CLK), a 4-bit data input (DATA_IN), and a 4-bit data output (DATA_OUT). When WE is high on a rising edge of the clock, the data from DATA_IN should be stored in the memory. When WE is low, the data from the memory should be output to DATA_OUT on the next rising edge of the clock.
code:
module dram_cell (
    input wire clk,
    input wire we,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    reg [3:0] memory;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (we) begin
            memory <= data_in; // Write data to memory

endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit divider that takes a dividend and a divisor as inputs and produces a quotient and a remainder as outputs. The design should handle division by zero gracefully by returning a default value for quotient and remainder.

Design a 2-bit shift register with asynchronous reset. The shift register should have two inputs: 'data_in' for input data and 'shift' signal to trigger the shifting operation. When 'shift' is high, the register should shift the bits to the right, and 'data_in' should be loaded into the leftmost bit. If 'reset' is high, the register should reset to '00'. The output of the register should be available as 'data_out'.
code:
module shift_register_2bit (

    input wire reset,  
    input wire shift,  
    input wire data_in,  
    output reg [1:0] data_out  
);  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            data_out <= 2'b00;  
        end else if (shift) begin

description: Design a 32-bit serializer that takes a 32-bit input data and serially shifts it out bit by bit on a clock edge. The output should be a single bit that represents the serialized data, and a counter should be included to track how many bits have been serialized. The serializer should reset when a reset signal is asserted.

Design a 32-bit CRC generator using the polynomial \( x^{32} + x^{26} + x^{23} + x^{22} + x^{16} + x^{12} + x^{11} + x^{10} + x^{8} + x^{7} + x^{5} + x^{4} + x^{2} + x^{1} + 1 \). Design a 32-bit timer that counts up every clock cycle and can be reset asynchronously. The timer output should be a 32-bit value that represents the current count. The timer should also have an enable input to start or stop the counting. Implement the following inputs and outputs:
- Input: clk (clock), rst (reset), en (enable)
- Output: count (32-bit timer value)

module Timer (

    input wire rst,
    input wire en,
    output reg [31:0] count

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            count <= 32'b0;
        end else if (en) begin
            count <= count + 1;
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 5-stage pipelined processor that can perform addition and subtraction operations based on an operation code (opcode). The pipeline should include stages: Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Execute (EX), Memory Access (MEM), and Write Back (WB). Design a Verilog module that implements an HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) using a simple XOR operation for the inner and outer padding. Design a simple audio compressor that reduces the amplitude of input audio samples when they exceed a certain threshold. The compressor will have a threshold input and an audio sample input, and it will output the compressed audio sample based on the threshold.

Design a simple echo cancellation module that takes an input signal and a reference signal (echo), and generates an output signal that cancels the echo from the input signal. The module should have a clock and reset signal, and should store the previous input signal to perform the cancellation.

Create a simple NAT (Network Address Translation) module that translates a private IP address to a public IP address. The module should have an input for a private IP address (32-bits) and an input for a translation request signal. When the translation request signal is high, the module should output the corresponding public IP address based on a predefined mapping. The mapping can be implemented using a simple case statement.
code:
module nat_translation (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [31:0] private_ip,
    input wire request,
    output reg [31:0] public_ip
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            public_ip <= 32'b0;
        end else if (request) begin
            case (private_ip)
                32'hC0A80001: public_ip <= 32'h1A2B3C4D; // 192.168.0.1 -> 26.43.60.77
                32'hC0A80002: public_ip <= 32'h1A2B3C4E; // 192.168.0.2 -> 26.43.60.78
                32'hC0A80003: public_ip <= 32'h1A2B3C4F; // 192.168.0.3 -> 26.43.60.79
                32'hC0A80004: public_ip <= 32'h1A2B3C50; // 192.168.0.4 -> 26.43.60.80
                default: public_ip <= 32'hFFFFFFFF; // Unknown
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a current sensor data logging system that captures the current readings from a sensor at regular intervals defined by a clock signal. The system should include a 4-bit counter that increments every time a new reading is taken. The current sensor data is 8 bits wide.

A digital phase shifter that takes an input clock signal and produces an output clock signal that is phase-shifted by a specified number of clock cycles. The phase shift will be controlled by a 2-bit input value that determines how many clock cycles to shift the output signal.
code:
module phase_shifter (
    input clk,
    input [1:0] phase_ctrl, // 2-bit control for phase shift
    output reg shifted_clk
);
    reg [1:0] counter;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (counter == phase_ctrl) begin
            shifted_clk <= ~shifted_clk; // Toggle the output clock
            counter <= 0; // Reset counter
        end else begin
            counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
        end
    end

    initial begin
        shifted_clk = 0; // Initialize output clock
        counter = 0; // Initialize counter
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 4-bit SRAM cell that allows writing data into the memory and reading it back. The SRAM cell should have an input data line, a read/write control signal, and an output data line. The read/write control signal will determine whether the cell is in read mode or write mode. When in write mode, the input data should be stored in the cell, and when in read mode, the stored data should be output.

Design a PID controller in Verilog that takes an error signal and produces a control signal. The controller should have three adjustable parameters: proportional gain (Kp), integral gain (Ki), and derivative gain (Kd). The PID controller should update its output on every clock cycle based on the current error input and maintain an internal state for the integral and derivative calculations.

Create a Verilog module that implements a simple gradient descent algorithm to minimize a quadratic function. The function can be defined as f(x) = (x - 3)^2. The module should take an initial value for x and a learning rate, then update x using the gradient descent formula: x = x - learning_rate * (2*(x - 3)).
code:
module gradient_descent(
    input clock,
    input reset,
    input [15:0] initial_x,
    input [15:0] learning_rate,
    output reg [15:0] current_x
);
    
    always @(posedge clock or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            current_x <= initial_x;
        end else begin
            current_x <= current_x - (learning_rate * (2 * (current_x - 16'd3))) >> 16; // Shift to maintain precision
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a state-space controller in Verilog that has a 2-bit state register and takes a 2-bit input signal. The controller should have the following states: 00 (Idle), 01 (Processing), 10 (Complete), and 11 (Error). The transitions between states are defined as follows: 
- If in Idle (00) and input is 01, transition to Processing (01).
- If in Processing (01) and input is 10, transition to Complete (10).
- If in Complete (10) and input is 11, transition to Error (11).
- If in Error (11) and input is 00, return to Idle (00).
- For any other cases, remain in the current state.

Design an 8x Phase Locked Loop (PLL) circuit in Verilog that takes a reference clock signal as input and generates an output clock signal that is 8 times the frequency of the reference clock. The output clock should have a 50% duty cycle. Implement the behavior using a D flip-flop and a counter to divide the clock frequency appropriately.
code:
module pll_8x (
    input wire clk_ref,      // Reference clock input
    input wire reset,        // Asynchronous reset
    output reg clk_out       // Output clock
);
    reg [2:0] counter;       // 3-bit counter for 8x division

    always @(posedge clk_ref or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 3'b0;
            clk_out <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (counter == 3'b111) begin // Counter reaches 7
                clk_out <= ~clk_out;     // Toggle clock output
                counter <= 3'b0;          // Reset counter
            end else begin
                counter <= counter + 1;   // Increment counter
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a Verilog module that performs LU decomposition on a 2x2 matrix. The input to the module will be a 2x2 matrix represented as two 8-bit inputs (A and B) for the two rows of the matrix, and the output will be the two matrices L and U also represented as two 8-bit outputs (L and U) for each row. The matrix A is given as:  
A = | a11 a12 |  
    | a21 a22 |  
The output should be:  
L = | l11 0   |  
    | l21 l22 |  
U = | u11 u12 |  
    | 0   u22 |  
Where:  
l11 = a11,  
l21 = a21/a11,  
u11 = a11,  
u12 = a12,  
u22 = a22 - l21 * u12.

Design a Verilog module that implements a simple finite state machine (FSM) for a light controller. The FSM should have three states: OFF, ON, and BLINK. The module should transition between these states based on two inputs: a clock signal and a control signal. The control signal will dictate the transitions: 
- If the control signal is 0, the state remains the same.
- If the control signal is 1, the FSM should toggle between ON and OFF states.
- In ON state, if the control signal is 2, the FSM should transition to BLINK state, which will toggle the light output every clock cycle.
The module should have a single output that indicates the state of the light (1 for ON, 0 for OFF, and 2 for BLINK).

Design a Viterbi decoder for a convolutional code with a constraint length of 3 and a generator polynomial of (7,5) in octal. The decoder should accept a sequence of received bits and produce the most likely sequence of original bits as output using the Viterbi algorithm. Ensure that your implementation can handle a sequence of up to 15 bits.

Design a simple OFDM modulator that takes in a stream of data bits (for example, 8 bits) and generates a corresponding symbol stream. The modulator should use a simple mapping scheme where each 8-bit input results in a corresponding 4-symbol output using a predefined mapping. Implement a register-based state machine to handle the input data and generate the output symbols.

Design a 4-input priority arbiter in Verilog. The arbiter should take four request signals (req0, req1, req2, req3) and output a grant signal (granted) indicating which request has the highest priority. The priority is from req0 (highest) to req3 (lowest). Only one grant should be active at any time.

Design an 8-bit serializer that takes an 8-bit input and serializes it into a single output bit stream. The serializer should shift out one bit every clock cycle, starting from the least significant bit (LSB) to the most significant bit (MSB). The process should be controlled by a start signal that indicates when to begin serialization. When serialization is complete, an output signal should indicate that the serialization process is done.
code:
module serializer (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg serial_out,
    output reg done
);
    reg [2:0] bit_counter; // 3 bits to count 0-7
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            bit_counter <= 3'b000;
            shift_reg <= 8'b0;
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
            done <= 1'b0;
        end else if (start) begin
            shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data into shift register
            bit_counter <= 3'b000; // Reset the bit counter
            done <= 1'b0; // Reset done signal
        end else if (bit_counter < 3'b1000) begin // If not all bits are serialized
            serial_out <= shift_reg[bit_counter]; // Output the current bit
            bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1; // Increment bit counter
        end else begin
            done <= 1'b1; // Signal that serialization is done
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a 4-point FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) module in Verilog that takes 4 complex input samples and computes the 4-point FFT. The inputs will be two 4-bit real parts and two 4-bit imaginary parts for each of the 4 complex numbers. The outputs should be similarly structured, with the real and imaginary parts of the transformed complex numbers. You need to handle the FFT stages and utilize a sequential logic approach to manage the calculations and state transitions.

Design a SRT (Sweeney, Robertson, and Tocher) divider in Verilog. The divider should take a 16-bit dividend and a 16-bit divisor as inputs and output a 16-bit quotient and a 16-bit remainder. You should implement the division algorithm using an SRT method, which allows for more efficient division than traditional methods.

Design a simple Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) in Verilog that consists of a phase detector, a low-pass filter, and a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO). The PLL should take an input clock signal and a reference clock signal, and generate an output clock signal that is phase-locked to the reference clock. The output frequency of the VCO should be adjustable based on the control voltage generated from the low-pass filter. The phase detector should output a pulse width proportional to the phase difference between the input and reference clock signals.

Design a 24-bit digital to analog converter (DAC) that takes a 24-bit binary input and outputs a 24-bit binary equivalent. The DAC will output the same value as the input, essentially acting as a pass-through mechanism for this problem.

Design a 4-bit ripple-carry adder that takes two 4-bit binary numbers and a carry-in as inputs, and outputs a 4-bit sum and a carry-out. The adder should be implemented using basic logic gates and should support addition of the two numbers.
Create a JK latch in Verilog with enable control. The latch should output the current state based on the J and K inputs when the enable signal is high. Otherwise, it should hold its current state.

Design a 16-bit ADC (Analog to Digital Converter) output decoder. The decoder should take the 16-bit input from the ADC and classify it into four ranges. The output should be a 2-bit code that indicates which range the input falls into: 
- 00 for 0-4095, 
- 01 for 4096-8191, 
- 10 for 8192-12287, 
- 11 for 12288-65535.

Design a 16-bit DAC (Digital-to-Analog Converter) in Verilog. The DAC takes a 16-bit binary input and produces a 16-bit output representing the analog value. The output should be the same as the input as this is a simple model of a DAC where the digital value is directly mapped to the output.

description: Design a convolutional encoder that takes a 2-bit input and produces a 4-bit output using the following polynomial representation: g1(x) = 1 + x + x^2 and g2(x) = 1 + x^2. The encoder should have a constraint length of 3 and use a shift register to store the input bits.

Design a Serial-In Parallel-Out (SIPO) shift register in Verilog. The register should accept a serial input bit and shift it into the register on each clock cycle. Once the register is filled, it should output the contents in parallel on a specific output signal.
code:
module sipo_shift_register (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input serial_in,
    output reg [4:0] parallel_out
);
    reg [4:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            shift_reg <= 5'b0; // Reset shift register
        end else begin
            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[3:0], serial_in}; // Shift left and insert new bit
        end
    end

    always @* begin
        parallel_out = shift_reg; // Output parallel data
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit 2-to-1 multiplexer. The multiplexer has two 8-bit data inputs (A and B), a select input (S), and an 8-bit output (Y). When S is 0, Y should output A, and when S is 1, Y should output B.

Design a module that performs a Monte Carlo simulation for generating random numbers. The module should take a seed value as input and output a pseudo-random number. The output should be obtained using a simple linear feedback shift register (LFSR) method, where the seed is processed to generate the next random number. The output should be 5 bits wide.

Create a divide-by-2 circuit using flip-flops. The circuit should take a single-bit binary input and output the result of dividing the input by 2. The output should be valid on the rising edge of a clock signal, and the input should be valid on the falling edge of the clock signal.
code:
module divide_by_2(  
    input clk,  
    input rst_n,  
    input in,  
    output reg out  
);  
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin  
        if (!rst_n) begin  
            out <= 1'b0;  
        end else begin  
            out <= in;  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a 32-bit ALU that can perform addition, subtraction, bitwise AND, bitwise OR, and bitwise XOR operations based on a 3-bit opcode input. The ALU should take two 32-bit inputs and provide a 32-bit output.
code:
module ALU_32bit(  
    input [31:0] A,  
    input [31:0] B,  
    input [2:0] opcode,  
    output reg [31:0] result  
);

            default: result = 32'b0;        // Default case  
        endcase  
    end  
endmodule

Design a 64-bit comparator that compares two 64-bit unsigned integers and outputs:
- 1 if the first integer is greater than the second,
- 0 if they are equal,
- -1 if the first integer is less than the second.

Design a simple Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier in Verilog that can take two 4-bit inputs representing two features and classify them into one of two classes based on a linear decision boundary. The output should be a single bit indicating the class (0 or 1). The decision boundary can be defined by the equation: w1 * x1 + w2 * x2 > threshold, where w1 = 1, w2 = 1, and threshold = 5.
code:
module svm_classifier (
    input [3:0] feature1,
    input [3:0] feature2,
    output reg class_out
);
    
    parameter w1 = 4'b0001;  // weight for feature1
    parameter w2 = 4'b0001;  // weight for feature2
    parameter threshold = 4'b0101; // threshold (5 in decimal)
    
    always @(*) begin
        if ((feature1 * w1 + feature2 * w2) > threshold)
            class_out = 1'b1; // Class 1
        else
            class_out = 1'b0; // Class 0
    end
endmodule

description:
Design an SPI master controller that can send and receive data to/from an SPI slave device. The SPI master should have the following specifications:
- Clock generation for SPI communication.
- Ability to send a byte of data (8 bits) to the slave.
- Ability to receive a byte of data from the slave.
- Control signals: `SCLK`, `MOSI`, `MISO`, and `SS` (Slave Select).
- The controller should operate in a simple mode: when the `start` signal is high, it should begin the transmission of a byte and then receive a byte back from the slave.
code:
module spi_master (
    input clk,
    input start,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg SCLK,
    output reg MOSI,
    output reg SS,
    input MISO
);
    reg [3:0] bit_count;
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;
    reg state; // 0: idle, 1: sending, 2: receiving

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            0: begin // idle
                SS <= 1; // deselect slave
                if (start) begin
                    state <= 1;
                    bit_count <= 0;
                    shift_reg <= data_in;
                    SS <= 0; // select slave
                end
            end
            1: begin // sending
                SCLK <= ~SCLK; // toggle clock
                if (SCLK) begin
                    MOSI <= shift_reg[7]; // send MSB first
                    shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // shift left
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                    if (bit_count == 7) begin
                        state <= 2; // go to receiving
                    end
                end
            end
            2: begin // receiving
                SCLK <= ~SCLK; // toggle clock
                if (SCLK) begin
                    data_out <= {data_out[6:0], MISO}; // receive bit
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                    if (bit_count == 7) begin
                        SS <= 1; // deselect slave
                        state <= 0; // go back to idle
                    end
                end
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

module crc_generator (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    input data_valid,
    output reg [7:0] crc_out
);

    reg [3:0] bit_count;

    // Polynomial for CRC-8: x^8 + x^7 + x^6 + x^4 + x^3 + 1
    localparam POLYNOMIAL = 8'h1D; // 00011101 in binary

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            crc <= 8'hFF; // Initial value
            bit_count <= 0;
            crc_out <= 8'h00;
        end else if (data_valid && bit_count < 8) begin
            crc[7:0] <= crc[7:0] ^ data_in[7:0]; // XOR with input data
            for (bit_count = 0; bit_count < 8; bit_count = bit_count + 1) begin
                if (crc[7]) begin
                    crc <= {crc[6:0], 1'b0} ^ POLYNOMIAL; // Shift and XOR with polynomial
                end else begin
                    crc <= {crc[6:0], 1'b0}; // Just shift
                end
            end
            crc_out <= crc; // Output the CRC
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment bit count
        end
    end
endmodule
